skillSays: Load three.js as ES modules through an import map; no script-tag builds.
Set up the renderer deliberately: capped pixel ratio, tone mapping, PCFShadowMap (the soft variant is deprecated), resize with updateProjectionMatrix.
Drive the loop with renderer.setAnimationLoop and a Timer (Clock is deprecated), and ease with frame-rate independent MathUtils.damp.
Use InstancedMesh for repeated objects and merge static geometry; keep draw calls low.
Procedural motion for simple scenes; AnimationMixer clips only for authored animation.
Dispose geometry, materials and textures, and release the renderer, when the scene goes away.

changes: The 24 appointment slots are one InstancedMesh (one draw call) with per-instance color, instead of 24 separate meshes
All easing (slots filling, pointer parallax) uses MathUtils.damp on a Timer delta, so it feels the same at 30 and 120 fps; the Timer also pauses while the tab is hidden

Physical materials get an image-based light built once from a tiny PMREM studio scene, then disposed; pagehide frees geometry, materials, environment and renderer; reduced motion draws one settled frame
Particles are a single Points object whose dynamic position buffer is updated per frame; settle progress is damped toward a target that time and scroll both push
Pixel ratio is capped at 2, fog fades the distant cloud, and the sprite texture is a CanvasTexture created once and disposed on pagehide
Camera framing is computed from aspect and field of view so the grid fits at any width; reduced motion jumps straight to the settled grid

notes: Pinned to three@0.170.0 per the brief: Timer comes from three/addons/misc/Timer.js (core Timer arrived later) and its connect() is optional-chained.
